mappings.note: Names the parent work (Yashodhara) the extract is drawn from -- placing a text in its source composition, not hunting a detail inside it. Rejected C-HIN2.2-LO-2, which is the in-text specific-point search.
Poet attribution -- bibliographic framing of the composition. Rejected C-HIN2.2-LO-2: the poet's name is not a point found by examining the verse closely.
Who narrates -- a specific point located by close reading of the dialogue. Rejected C-HIN2.2-LO-1: nothing about the text's overall usefulness is asked.
Who listens -- the paired close-reading detail to the narrator item. Rejected C-HIN2.1-LO-1: no agreement or own-experience response is invited.
Identifies the referent of the address 'taat' -- a specific point recovered from the text. Rejected C-HIN4.1-LO-1: 'taat' is glossed by the narrative, not tested as new vocabulary here.
Character name retrieval. Rejected C-HIN2.2-LO-1, which covers gist rather than a named detail.
Character name retrieval. Rejected C-HIN2.2-LO-1 for the same reason as the preceding item.

Siddhartha's later name -- a point the poem supplies by implication and the reader must locate. Rejected C-HIN3.1-LO-1: the Buddha legend here is literary narrative, not the learner's own folk repertoire.
Who lifted the swan -- plot detail. Rejected C-HIN2.1-LO-1: the act's moral worth is asked elsewhere; this item only asks who.
Who shot the swan -- plot detail. Rejected C-HIN1.2-LO-2: the item does not ask the learner to react to the cruelty, only to report it.
Why the wounded-bird episode is in the poem at all -- the function and usefulness of the whole passage. Rejected C-HIN2.2-LO-2, which is detail-finding, not purpose.
Attributes one of four quoted lines to the mother -- exactly a close examination for a specific point. Rejected C-HIN2.1-LO-1: no evaluation of the idea is required.
Cause of the swan's fall, stated in the verse. Rejected C-HIN2.2-LO-1: a single narrative fact, not the text's utility.
What the father did on seeing the bird -- plot detail. Rejected C-HIN2.1-LO-1, reserved here for items that ask the learner to weigh the deed.
Where the dispute ended up -- plot detail. Rejected C-HIN2.2-LO-1: no gist judgement involved.

Rahul's own criterion for true justice -- understanding the idea the poet puts in a character's mouth and what it commits him to. Rejected C-HIN2.2-LO-2: the answer is a reasoned position, not a locatable fact.
The verdict Rahul gives, as stated. Rejected C-HIN2.1-LO-1: the neighbouring item already asks for the reasoning; this one asks only for the decision.
Infers a character trait from the line 'nyaay daya ka daani' -- reading the poet's idea past its surface. Rejected C-HIN2.2-LO-2: the trait is nowhere written down to be found.
What the mother asked -- close reading of the dialogue. Rejected C-HIN1.1-LO-2: the learner is not framing questions, only recovering one.
What kind of story the mother told (religious/moral/historical/all) -- a judgement about the whole text's character and use. Rejected C-HIN2.2-LO-2: no single point answers it.
Which two parties quarrelled -- plot detail. Rejected C-HIN1.2-LO-1: the dispute is a narrative fact here, not a sensitive social issue to reason about.
Line completion with an ordinary word ('kahaani') -- it turns on recalling the verse, not on word knowledge. Rejected C-HIN4.1-LO-1, kept for the blanks whose missing word is genuinely unfamiliar.

Blank is 'cheti', an unfamiliar literary word for a maidservant -- the item tests the fine grain of the poem's diction. Rejected C-HIN2.2-LO-2: recalling the line is not enough without knowing the word.
Blank is 'nirbhay' -- a charged adverbial choice the learner must supply. Rejected C-HIN4.1-LO-2, which covers the learner's own writing, not filling the poet's line.
Blank is 'khagbhakshi', a compound the learner is unlikely to hold without attending to the poem's vocabulary. Rejected C-HIN2.2-LO-2 on the same reasoning as 'cheti'.
Blank is 'daya', an everyday word in the poem's best-known line -- verse recall. Rejected C-HIN4.1-LO-1: nothing lexically new is being tested.
Blank is 'aahat' -- a literary synonym for wounded that the learner must have taken from this text. Rejected C-HIN2.2-LO-2: the demand is lexical.
Blank is 'baani' (speech), an archaic form and the rhyme partner of 'kahaani'. Rejected C-HIN2.2-LO-2: word knowledge, not plot.
Blank is 'phool' -- plain vocabulary, so the item is verse recall. Rejected C-HIN4.1-LO-1 for lack of any lexical difficulty.
Short-answer restatement of who narrates. Rejected C-HIN4.2-LO-1: the answer is the text's, not the learner's own experience.
Who listens, short answer. Rejected C-HIN2.2-LO-1: a single point, not the text's usefulness.
Mother's name, short answer. Rejected C-HIN2.2-LO-1 as above.
Who lifted the wounded swan, short answer. Rejected C-HIN2.1-LO-1: no appraisal asked.
Whose side won -- outcome of the dispute as narrated. Rejected C-HIN2.1-LO-1: the moral reading of that outcome is a separate item.
'What is justice like' -- the poem's governing claim, which the learner must grasp and restate as a position. Rejected C-HIN2.2-LO-2: it is an idea, not a findable detail.
Poet attribution in short-answer form, with the 'rashtrakavi' epithet. Rejected C-HIN2.2-LO-2 for the same reason as the MCQ on authorship.
Who Rahul's father is -- relational detail from the text. Rejected C-HIN2.2-LO-1: not a gist item.
Siddhartha's famous name, short answer. Rejected C-HIN3.1-LO-1: literary narrative, not the learner's local folk material.
Where Siddhartha walked at dawn ('upavan') -- a small point recoverable only by careful reading. Rejected C-HIN3.2-LO-1: the garden is a setting, not craft or farming language.
Who shot the swan, short answer. Rejected C-HIN1.2-LO-2: reporting, not reacting.
Source composition of the extract, short answer. Rejected C-HIN2.2-LO-2: bibliographic placement rather than in-text detail.
What Rahul wanted of his mother -- opening situation of the poem. Rejected C-HIN2.1-LO-1: no evaluation required.
Cause of the swan's injury. Rejected C-HIN2.2-LO-1: narrative causation, not usefulness.
The mother's teasing remark about the grandmother -- close reading of a light exchange. Rejected C-HIN4.2-LO-2: the learner reports the remark, does not rewrite it.

The father's response to the bird, which the model answer frames as compassion and resistance -- the idea behind the act, not just the act. Rejected C-HIN2.2-LO-2, used for the bare 'who lifted it' item.
Why the matter reached court -- causal detail supplied by the narrative. Rejected C-HIN2.1-LO-1: no stance of the learner's own is invited.
Where 'taat' had gone walking. Rejected C-HIN2.2-LO-1: a single located point.
What the hunter demanded. Rejected C-HIN2.1-LO-1: the hunter's claim is weighed in a later item, not this one.
Whose side Rahul took, as stated. Rejected C-HIN2.1-LO-1: the reasoning behind the choice is a separate item.
Who Rahul is -- relational identification. Rejected C-HIN2.2-LO-1: detail, not gist.
What kind of justice the poem expects -- the poet's thesis, which the learner must articulate. Rejected C-HIN2.2-LO-2: no line states it outright.
What the maid said to Rahul -- close reading of a minor exchange. Rejected C-HIN4.1-LO-1: the archaic 'cheti' is tested lexically elsewhere.
Who Yashodhara's 'maandhan' is and how he behaves -- two located details. Rejected C-HIN2.1-LO-1: description, not appraisal.
How Rahul characterises the story of the lost wing, as the text reports it. Rejected C-HIN2.1-LO-1: the learner recovers his words rather than forming a view.
What the hunter resolved to insist on. Rejected C-HIN2.2-LO-1: a specific point, not the passage's use.
How the swan felt on being lifted -- the poem states it as new life. Rejected C-HIN2.1-LO-1: the feeling is given, not inferred.
Who saves the swan. Rejected C-HIN2.2-LO-1: bare detail.
Characterises the whole mother-son exchange as affectionate, curious and morally instructive -- a reading of the poet's design. Rejected C-HIN2.2-LO-2: no single point yields it.
What the hunter demanded and on what stated ground -- both are in the verse. Rejected C-HIN2.1-LO-1: the learner is not asked whether the ground is sound.
Why the mother was pleased -- requires reading her unstated approval of Rahul's moral grasp. Rejected C-HIN2.2-LO-2: the reason is inferred, not located.
